who: Historian of American women at Arizona State University; PhD, University of California, Riverside (ASU lists 1983).

evidence.says: ASU identifies Gayle Gullett as a history professor, lists a Riverside PhD in 1983, and names Becoming Citizens among her works.
The authority for Gayle Ann Gullett records the usage Gayle Gullett on Becoming Citizens and Gayle Ann Gullett on Feminism, politics, and voluntary groups (1983).
The 2005-2006 graduate catalog lists Gayle Gullett as associate professor of history, appointed in 1993, with a Riverside PhD.

notes: Name usage, book and institution identify the candidate. The AHA doctorate year is 1982; ASU gives 1983, a discrepancy retained here.

who: Historian of women and modern France at the University of Maryland; PhD, North Carolina, Chapel Hill, 1978.

evidence.says: Maryland identifies Gay L. Gullickson as history professor emerita, author of Spinners and Weavers of Auffay and Unruly Women of Paris, and director of undergraduate studies in 1997-2000.
The faculty catalog lists Gay L. Gullickson in History with a 1978 PhD from the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill.
The Gay L. Gullickson authority cites Spinners and weavers of Auffay (1986), identifying its author with the University of Maryland, and Unruly women of Paris (1996).

notes: The authority explicitly supplies the student institution, and the doctoral institution and year match exactly.

who: European intellectual historian at Duke University, publishing as Malachi Haim Hacohen; PhD, Columbia, 1993.

evidence.says: Duke gives the full name Malachi Haim Hacohen, identifies him as professor of history and Bass Fellow since 2006, lists Columbia PhD 1993, and attributes Karl Popper: The Formative Years to him.
The Malachi Haim Hacohen authority is established from Karl Popper, the formative years, 1902-1945 (2000).

notes: Full name, distinctive book, Duke affiliation and Columbia doctorate agree.

who: Historian of modern Germany at Stony Brook University; PhD, Michigan, Ann Arbor, 1989.

evidence.says: Young-Sun Hong lists Stony Brook appointments from 1993 onward and a 1989 PhD from Michigan, Ann Arbor; publications concern German welfare and Cold War history.
Stony Brook identifies Young-Sun Hong as professor of history specializing in modern Germany and author of Welfare, Modernity and the Weimar State.
The authority heading is Hong, Young-Sun, with a source citation beginning The contradictions of modernity and the ... (1998).

notes: The distinctive name, German-history field, student institution and exact Michigan doctorate agree.

who: Military historian at the University of Georgia; PhD in history, University of Virginia.

evidence.says: The contributor biography identifies Lee Kennett as Georgia history professor, with a Virginia history PhD, and author of A History of Strategic Bombing.
The 1976 AHA meeting program lists Lee Kennett, University of Georgia, speaking on French participation in the American Revolution.
The Lee Kennett authority cites A history of strategic bombing (1983) and The French armies in the Seven Years’ War (1967).

notes: The same book links the authority to the Georgia professor; the 1976 affiliation falls within the listed supervision period. The doctorate institution agrees; its year was not independently confirmed.

who: US intellectual and cultural historian at the University of California, Berkeley; PhD in history, UCLA.

evidence.says: Berkeley identifies Kerwin L. Klein as history professor emeritus, with a UCLA history PhD, and lists Frontiers of Historical Imagination and From History to Theory.
The 2011 book page gives the full name Kerwin Lee Klein and identifies its author as professor of history at Berkeley and author of Frontiers of Historical Imagination.
The Kerwin Lee Klein authority is established from Frontiers of historical imagination (1997).

notes: Full name and books bridge the authority to Berkeley during the student years; UCLA agrees. The AHA doctorate year was not independently confirmed.

who: Elizabeth Clark-Lewis, Howard University historian and public-history program director; PhD, University of Maryland, College Park.

evidence.says: In an interview, listed student Ashley Jordan identifies her graduate-school advisor as Dr. Elizabeth Clark-Lewis of Howard University.
Clark-Lewis’s institutional CV lists a Maryland PhD, Howard appointments from 1990 onward, and directorship of the Public History Program.
The supplied authority identifies Elizabeth Wittenmyer Lewis as the author of Queen of the Confederacy (2002).
The publisher identifies Elizabeth Wittenmyer Lewis as the author of Queen of the Confederacy, lists nursing education at Jefferson Medical School and further study at Rice University.

notes: The student identifies Clark-Lewis, a different author from candidate p-100891. The supplied Georgetown 1975 doctorate also conflicts with Clark-Lewis’s institutional CV and appears to be a conflated record.

who: Daniel C. Littlefield, historian of slavery and colonial America at the University of South Carolina; PhD, Johns Hopkins.

evidence.says: South Carolina names Daniel C. Littlefield as advisor to Rachel Monroy (2015), Margaret Gillikin and Tyler Parry (2014), and Justin Liles (2011), matching listed students and dissertation topics.
His faculty page gives a Johns Hopkins PhD, a South Carolina appointment since August 1999, and authorship of Rice and Slaves (1981).
The Daniel C. Littlefield authority cites Rice and slaves (1981) and a later source identifying him as history and Black Studies professor at Illinois.
The separate scholar Daniel F. Littlefield is identified with the Sequoyah National Research Center, the University of Arkansas at Little Rock, and an Oklahoma State PhD.

notes: Direct advisor evidence establishes Daniel C., candidate p-131151. Daniel F., candidate p-129777, is a different scholar. Johns Hopkins agrees; the supplied 1977 doctorate year was not independently confirmed.
